study_identification.author_journal_year: Mansour L., S. et al., medRxiv, 2025
study_identification.title: Spectral normative modeling of brain structure

study_characteristics.study_objective: To introduce and validate a novel spectral normative modeling (SNM) framework that leverages brain eigenmodes to efficiently generate normative ranges for brain structure at multiple spatial scales, overcoming limitations of conventional methods.

dataset_name.answer: HCP Young Adult; HCP Aging; HCP Development

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer (versions 5.2 and 6.0); HCP minimal preprocessing pipeline; MSMAll

quality_checking_detail.answer: The HCP minimal preprocessing pipeline includes gradient distortion correction, skull stripping, readout distortion correction, and bias field correction. FreeSurfer processing includes surface reconstruction and registration. No explicit mention of participant exclusion based on QC metrics in the main text, but the pipelines are standard and validated.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) was used to model site effects as random effects. The model included intercepts for the mean (βμ) and deviation (β+σ) that were randomly drawn from a prior distribution, effectively creating a hierarchical model for batch effects (dataset harmonization).

modeling_method.answer: Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR); Spectral Normative Modeling (SNM)

software_tool.answer: PyMC; scikit-learn; Numpy; Scipy; Matplotlib; Pandas; Nibabel; Cerebro

predictor_effects.answer: Age and Sex were modeled as fixed effects. Site was modeled as a random effect (hierarchical).

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study explicitly models site effects, which are a major source of nuisance variance, using Hierarchical Bayesian Regression. This approach accounts for mean and variance shifts across different datasets (HCP-D, HCP-YA, HCP-A).
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Moreover, batch effects were included in the model to facilitate harmonization among the three imaging cohorts (development, young adult, and aging). ... Batch effects (for dataset harmonization) are modeled as intercepts for the mean ( β µ ∼ N ( µ β µ , σ β µ ) ) and deviation ( β + σ ∼ N ( µ β + σ , σ 2 β + σ ) ) that are randomly drawn from another prior distribution; this results in hierarchically modeling batch as a random effect.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study uses a train-test split for validation. The model is trained on 80% of the data and evaluated on the remaining 20% (held-out set). There is no mention of validation on the training set itself.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Healthy individuals were stratified into train and test splits to enable validation of the fitted models on unseen data. Namely, 80% ( N train =1978 individuals) of the healthy data were used to train the model, and the remaining 20% ( N test =495) were used for out-of-sample validation...

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study uses a held-out test set (20% of the healthy data) for out-of-sample validation. This is a standard method for assessing model performance on independent data from the same domain.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Healthy individuals were stratified into train and test splits to enable validation of the fitted models on unseen data. Namely, 80% ( N train =1978 individuals) of the healthy data were used to train the model, and the remaining 20% ( N test =495) were used for out-of-sample validation...

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The model, pre-trained on the HCP dataset, was fine-tuned and applied to an independent clinical dataset (MACC) to assess its generalizability and clinical utility in a different population (elderly individuals with and without cognitive impairment).
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Next, we demonstrate the practical utility of SNM by applying it to an independent clinical sample. Specifically, we analyze deviations in cortical thickness in an independent imaging dataset comprising three elderly cohorts of individuals with no cognitive impairment (healthy controls, HC, N=132), mild cognitive impairments (MCI, N=202), and Alzheimer’s Disease (AD, N=208)...

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group-level comparisons (t-tests) of deviation maps between HC and AD. Pearson correlation between vertex-wise z-scores and MMSE scores. Pearson correlation between ETVC and MMSE scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The proposed SNM method efficiently and accurately generates multi-scale normative brain charts, and its application to a clinical cohort reveals high-resolution cortical atrophy patterns in Alzheimer's disease that are associated with cognitive impairment.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: SNM achieves comparable accuracy to conventional direct models with a 98.3% speedup. It successfully generated high-resolution normative charts of cortical thickness across the lifespan. In a clinical application, SNM identified a cortical signature of atrophy in AD, characterized by widespread thinning in temporal, parietal, and frontal lobes. An extreme value statistic, ETVC, derived from the high-resolution deviation maps, was a strong predictor of cognitive impairment (MMSE scores, r = -0.45, p < 0.0001). The study also highlighted the heterogeneous nature of individual atrophy patterns in AD.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The current model assumes Gaussianity of the data, which might not hold for all phenotypes. The approach's validity depends on the assumption that the phenotype is well-captured by the low-frequency eigenmodes. The choice of the specific connectome eigenmodes and Laplacian operator, while justified, is one of many possibilities.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: SNM's ability to perform a posteriori queries on pre-trained models increases accessibility and facilitates federated learning. The method can be extended to other modalities and volumetric data. It also allows for the investigation of cortical asymmetry.

general_notes.general_notes: The paper introduces a novel concept of a 'spatial normative query' which allows for flexible assessment of normative ranges across arbitrary regions. The code for the framework is promised to be made openly available.
